claim: RLHF substantially reduces per-input output diversity compared to SFT across multiple externally-validated diversity metrics (syntactic, semantic, and logical), in both summarisation and instruction-following settings.
stance_target: output-diversity loss under RLHF as a rival mechanism explaining single-template collapse in LLM generation tasks
scope_conditions: LLaMA-7B base model, summarisation (TL;DR) and instruction-following (AlpacaFarm) tasks
quoted_support: However, RLHF significantly reduces output diversity compared to SFT across a variety of measures, implying a tradeoff in current LLM fine-tuning methods between generalisation and diversity.
numbers: 5 OPT model sizes tested in Appendix J

claim: The authors claim theirs is the first rigorous empirical demonstration of across-input mode collapse emerging specifically from RLHF training, where models trained with RLHF produce more similar outputs even across different inputs, not just repeated samples for the same input.
stance_target: mode collapse under RLHF as a documented, prior-published phenomenon (bears on novelty question: RLHF-diversity-loss is NOT a novel finding as of 2023-2024)
scope_conditions: LLaMA-7B and OPT models, summarisation task specifically (diversity effects not observed for instruction-following outputs due to metric length confounds)
quoted_support: We believe that this is the first rigorous empirical demonstration of across-input mode collapse emerging from RLHF training specifically.

claim: The RLHF diversity-loss effect (both per-input and across-input) replicates across all five tested OPT model scales, indicating the effect in this paper's data is not confined to a single model size and does not simply vanish or reverse as scale changes.
stance_target: whether output-diversity loss under RLHF is model-scale dependent
scope_conditions: OPT model family, summarisation task, five model sizes tested in Appendix J.4
quoted_support: Both these trends are the same for OPT across model sizes (see Section J.4 for full results)

claim: Increasing the KL penalty coefficient in RLHF training (which pulls the policy closer to the more-diverse SFT reference policy) reduces performance as expected but also reduces per-input diversity rather than restoring it, undermining a simple explanation that diversity loss is just a function of distance from the base/SFT model.
stance_target: mechanistic explanation of why RLHF causes diversity loss / mode collapse
scope_conditions: RLHF summarisation models, KL penalty coefficient sweep, Appendix I
quoted_support: increasing the KL penalty coefficient leads to a drop in performance as expected, but also to a drop in per-input diversity, rather than a gain

claim: The paper frames the generalisation-diversity tradeoff as possibly fundamental to current RLHF fine-tuning methods rather than a fixable bug, and explicitly calls for future research into why RLHF reduces diversity, citing RL diversity-injection techniques as a possible remedy.
stance_target: whether mode collapse under RLHF is a solved/settled problem as of 2023-2024
quoted_support: It is unclear whether this tradeoff is a fundamental one in fine-tuning LLMs with RLHF or just demonstrates a deficiency in current methods... Future work should investigate why RLHF reduces the output diversity so much, and whether this diversity can be recovered without the loss of performance.
